## Findings
- claim-1: For every bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), the lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\) in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- claim-2: The source identifies the right-adjoined family as the conjugate family and notes that transposition would prove its minimality, without stating that result as a corollary. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- claim-3: The involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution and preserves Littlewood–Richardson coefficients under partition conjugation. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-491]
- claim-4: The right-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) minimally generates \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) for every bigrassmannian parameter tuple.
## Strategy
Establish the right-family minimality internally by conjugation. Let \(q=n-r\). The involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) induces
\[
\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r},
\]
since \(\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\nsubseteq r^q\). The accepted parameter-conjugation certificate sends \(v\) to a bigrassmannian \(v^\vee\) with parameters \((j,i,a,b)\), and sends the right-adjoined family for \(v\) bijectively to the lower-adjoined family for \(v^\vee\).

The right family generates \(J_v\), while the lower family minimally generates \(J_{v^\vee}\) by the source-backed lower-family theorem [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]. Hence the induced isomorphism carries \(J_v\) onto \(J_{v^\vee}\). A redundant right-family element would map to a redundant lower-family element, contradiction. The \(a=0\) case is singleton and is covered as well.

Thus the requested target—minimality of the right-adjoined family—is established internally, not as a separately source-stated theorem.

## Gaps
No mathematical gap in this conjugation reduction. The literature itself states this only as a suggested transposition, not a formal corollary [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840].

## Next
Record the proved right-family result only as an internal consequence of the lower-family theorem, quotient conjugation, and the accepted admissibility certificate.
